item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00171","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C10","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.91,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 plausibly supplied a material template for conditioning an agency's exercise of authority affecting foreign matters on review by both the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense. The child compresses and adapts C02's machinery: an agency receives authority, must obtain or undertake prior consultation with the same two Secretaries, and may not proceed where foreign-relations or national-defense objections arise. C10 and C18 contain related State–Defense coordination structures, but neither parallels the child's dual pre-action review and objection mechanism as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Administrator, prior to taking any action under the authority hereby conferred, shall first consult with the Secretary of State on matters affecting foreign relations, and with the Secretary of Defense on matters affecting national-defense interests","parent_excerpt":"after obtaining the favorable recommendations of the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense thereon, to issue to the applicant, as appropriate, a permit","explanation":"Both directives condition an empowered agency's action on prior review by the same two cabinet officers, divided according to foreign-relations and defense concerns."},{"child_excerpt":"shall not take any action which the Secretary of State determines to be in conflict with any international treaty or agreement ... or to be inconsistent with the successful conduct of the foreign relations of the United States, or which the Secretary of Defense determines to be inconsistent with the requirements of national defense","parent_excerpt":"the proper conduct of the foreign relations of the United States requires that executive permission be obtained ... In any case wherein the Federal Power Commission, the Secretary of State, and the Secretary of Defense cannot agree as to whether or not a permit should be issued","explanation":"The child adapts C02's State-and-Defense concurrence machinery into express prohibitions triggered by either Secretary's determination, retaining the same foreign-relations and national-defense policy categories."}]}
